This is the third part of lab 7. It assumes you've set up your AWS group, user, configured the CLI, set up and launched an EC2 instance. 

In this lab, we'll create an S3 bucket and pushed the penguin `vetiver` model data.[^lab7-part-02]

[^lab7-part-02]: If you haven't completed these steps, please see [Getting started with AWS](start-aws.qmd) and [EC2 Buckets](aws-ec2.qmd)

## Creating S3 buckets

We can use the `s3api` command to create the S3 bucket for the `penguin-vetiver-model-data`.

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3api create-bucket \
  --bucket penguin-vetiver-model-data \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --profile dev-deploy
```

These commands are pretty straightforward, but you can also read more in the documentation.[^aws-s3-buckets] Note that bucket names must be globally unique. The response from the API should be something like the following: 

```json
{
    "Location": "/penguin-vetiver-model-data",
    "BucketArn": "arn:aws:s3:::penguin-vetiver-model-data"
}
```

[^aws-s3-buckets]: Read more about creating S3 buckets in [Creating a general purpose bucket
](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html)

We can also see this in the dashboard by looking up **S3** resources: 

![General purpose S3 bucket](img/lab7-s3-bucket-dashboard.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'}

## Pushing the models to S3

Now that we've created an S3 bucket, we can push the respective Python/R model data into their locations. I'd like to keep the same `Python/` and `R/` respective folders, which I've displayed below:[^lab7-code-files]

```{verbatim}
Python/
├── Dockerfile
├── mod-api.py
├── model.py
├── models/
│   └── penguin_model/
│       └── 20260618T104900Z-91fdd/
│           ├── data.txt
│           └── penguin_model.joblib
├── my-db.duckdb
├── README.md
├── requirements-api.txt
└── requirements.txt

4 directories, 9 files

```

```{verbatim}
R/
├── Dockerfile
├── model.R
├── models/
│   └── penguin_model/
│       └── 20260709T053628Z-09946/
│           ├── data.txt
│           └── penguin_model.rds
├── my-db.duckdb
├── plumber.R
├── README.md
├── renv/
└── renv.lock

10 directories, 10 files
```

[^lab7-code-files]: These [code files](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab07) have been copied over from our [previous lab](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab06). 

### Python model

From the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: 

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3 cp Python/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ \
  --recursive \
  --profile dev-deploy
```

### R model 

From the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: 

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3 cp R/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ \
  --recursive \
  --profile dev-deploy
```

### Copy vs. sync

It might make more sense to use `sync` instead of copy. `sync` only uploads new/changed files, which might be better for repeated deploys:

**`Python/`**:

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3 sync Python/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ --profile dev-deploy
```

**`R/`**:

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3 sync R/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ --profile dev-deploy
```

### Verify

We can verify the model data has been put in the S3 bucket at the command line:

```{bash}
#| eval: false 
#| code-fold: false
aws s3 ls s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/ --recursive --profile dev-deploy
```

We can also see this in the dashboard under **Amazon S3** > **Buckets**

![Click to enlarge S3 bucket with penguin model data](img/lab7-s3-bucket-upload.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'}
